description: Expected Swipewalk findings for MainPage, per platform. Each finding is matched on rule, kind, role and label (label = accessible name or visible text). null for a platform means no finding is expected there; knownMiss documents a real problem the scanner cannot detect yet. Keys: 'android' and 'ios' for single scans; 'androidLargeText' for findings that need the 200% text-size capture. 'iosLargeText' (AX3, about 235%) is reference data only -- no acceptance test reads it yet, there is no saved iOS large-text fixture. Android findings with an 'atf:' rule id come from Google's Accessibility Test Framework via the instrumentation harness; tests/Swipewalk.Core.Tests/Fixtures/BuggyApp.Android now includes the harness's atf-harness.json sidecar alongside the uiautomator dump, so GroundTruthTests exercises the merge (Finding.AlsoReportedBy) as well as ATF-only findings. A second, smaller fixture (Fixtures/BuggyApp.Android.History, the 'Payment history' screen reached from MainPage) is not covered by this file -- it is scoped to MainPage only -- but is checked by its own test (GroundTruthTests.HistoryScreen_AtfBackArrowContrastFinding) for one ATF-only finding (the back arrow's ImageContrastCheck) that only appears on that screen.

expected.element: City seal image, no text alternative
Decorative divider hidden from assistive technology
expected.note: Neither uiautomator nor XCUITest exposes the 'hidden on purpose' flag, so it is reported for review like B1. Also flagged by Google's Accessibility Test Framework (ImageContrastCheck, estimated ~2.09:1 against its background) via the Android instrumentation harness; reported for review under 1.4.11, which exempts purely decorative graphics, so a reviewer who confirms the divider is decorative should find no 1.4.11 problem here. Kept as a separate needsReview finding, not merged into missing-name, since it's a different concern (contrast vs. name) -- see RuleRunner.SameConcern. Seen in a live scan of the emulator on 2026-09-23.

expected.element: Icon-only search button with no name
Plate number entry, visible label not associated
Ticket number entry renders 44 dp tall on Android
expected.note: Resolved by the .NET MAUI version bump (BuggyApp pinned to 10.0.110, checked 2026-09-22): dotnet/maui#37151 ('SemanticProperties.Description is not applied to Android contentDescription for Entry', fixed .NET 10 SR11) means the uiautomator dump now shows content-desc="Ticket number" on this field, so missing-name no longer fires on Android at all (confirmed by a live scan, not just the saved fixture). Previously (MAUI 10.0.100 and earlier) content-desc was empty and 'Ticket number' appeared only in the rendered text attribute -- the same attribute a typed value would use -- so missing-name reported it for review (see KnownLimitations 'android-edittext-text', which still applies to fields without an explicit SemanticProperties.Description). On iOS this Entry's SemanticProperties.Description becomes a real accessibilityLabel ('Ticket number'), so it is named there and produces no missing-name finding either. The target-size advisory remains on Android, and Google's Accessibility Test Framework, via the Android instrumentation harness, flags this same field on two counts our own rules don't cover: EditableContentDescCheck (mapped to 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value -- the contentDescription the .NET MAUI #37151 fix now sets can stop TalkBack announcing what was typed instead) and DuplicateSpeakableTextCheck (no WCAG criterion is mapped -- the field's speakable text "Ticket number" is identical to another element's, probably the visible label above it). Seen in a live scan of the emulator on 2026-09-23. These two stay separate from target-size (different concern -- see RuleRunner.SameConcern); ATF's TouchTargetSizeCheck on this same field is the one that merges into target-size.

expected.element: Help icon drawn 20x20; MAUI enlarges the touch area to 44 dp/pt
Button shows 'Pay' but its name is 'Submit'
Close button with only an AutomationId (becomes resource-id / accessibilityIdentifier, not a name)
Tiny 'Terms' tap link next to the help button
expected.note: Not flagged under WCAG 2.5.8 on iOS because of the spacing exception.
expected.knownMissAndroid: MAUI does not mark tap-gesture labels as clickable, so uiautomator does not expose it as a target.

expected.element: 'Late fees apply after 30 days.' with a fixed 20 dp/pt height
expected.note: Only detectable with the large-text capture (record mode or scan --large-text). This is a fixed-height clipping bug (a text that never grows), not the live-update bug that TextResizeLiveUpdateRule reports -- the two are different and don't overlap. On iOS, before the app applied the larger text size live (BuggyApp now pins MAUI 10.0.110, which is past 10.0.100 / dotnet/maui#34445), almost every text on the screen failed to grow, so TextResizeRule's screen-level 'X of Y texts did not grow' finding covered B11 too instead of naming it (see case-study.md's 'B11 was covered by a broader finding'). Confirmed by a live scan on 2026-09-22 (MAUI 10.0.110): the screen-level finding is gone and B11 is now reported as its own per-text finding, same rule and kind, role and label as the Android large-text entry below. There is still no iOS large-text acceptance-test fixture (see the top-level description), so this is not yet enforced by GroundTruthTests.

expected.element: Navigation bar title from the default MAUI template styles (light gray on white)
Screen exposes no pane title to screen readers
expected.note: No pane title in the captured tree. MainPage sets Title="Parking tickets" (shown in the NavigationPage toolbar) and has two headings, but MAUI's Page.Title does not set an Android pane title. Whether TalkBack announces a screen title on arrival (e.g. from the window title, which this rule doesn't read) has not been checked. Android only (needs the instrumentation harness; AtfRan) -- not implemented on iOS. Added when the page-titled rule (WCAG 2.4.2) was introduced.

expected.element: Fixed font sizes do not follow the iOS text size setting
